issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is an undocumented semantic/contract change
issues.detail: The middleware now reads req.bounded_stream instead of req.stream with no argument, which is not a clean substitution: bounded_stream enforces Content-Length and behaves differently on malformed input. The PR description claims it adds req.content_length to req.stream.read(), so the diff disagrees with the commit message. Add a versionchanged note or comment justifying the swap.

issues.description: README handle() signature reordered to (req, resp, ex, params) without justification
issues.detail: The README snippet changes handle(ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params). This is an undocumented drive-by change in a PR titled 'add POST request tests' and should be verified against Falcon's current add_error_handler contract. Either justify it in the commit message or drop it from this PR.

issues.description: FAQ example handler has poor taste and unbounded read footgun
issues.detail: PostTest.on_post uses nested if/else where flat branches would do, and calls req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) with no upper bound, letting an attacker-supplied Content-Length trigger unbounded allocation. Since this is user-facing example code that readers copy, rewrite it cleanly and use bounded_stream or state the bound explicitly.

issues.description: PR bundles unrelated changes — split it
issues.detail: The stated goal is adding POST tests for things_advanced, but the diff also rewrites the README example (reformatting, signature change, str.format conversion, bounded_stream swap) and adds an FAQ entry. Reviewing is hard because the test addition is buried under reformatting noise. Land the tests cleanly and resubmit the README and FAQ work as separate PRs.

issues.description: FAQ test uses parenthesized assert which is a Python footgun
issues.detail: assert(result.status == ...) reads like a function call and trains readers toward the broken assert(x, y) form, which is always truthy. In canonical example code that teaches testing, write `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400` instead.

issues.description: New POST tests lack shared fixture and contract docstrings
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 hardcode the same Authorization and Content-Type headers with no shared dict, and assert status codes without naming which invariant of things_advanced is under test. A future maintainer reading a failure will not know whether the 400 is the spec or an accident. Extract common headers and add a one-line spec comment per assertion block.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the test additions themselves are useful but the PR has serious hygiene and contract-discipline issues. The most substantive problem, flagged by both reviewers, is the silent swap from req.stream to req.bounded_stream in the middleware — a contract change that contradicts the PR description and lacks a versionchanged note. Both reviewers also flag the unjustified README handle() signature reorder and the FAQ example's quality (nested branches plus an unbounded read pattern that readers will copy). The PR should be split: land the tests cleanly, resubmit README reformatting and the new FAQ entry as their own diffs with proper justification, and tighten the example code before it becomes canonical.
